title: Ring protocol records
notes: The data model is not on a ring. Core calls ta_datamodel_vtable synchronously, as today (reference/data-model.md). Only its results cross the rings, as value references.

Definition management uses request/result records. Native calls create and destroy the system, expose its rings, drive execution and install data model/value integrations. An attached debugger takes exclusive ownership of the whole system from the production pump. Inspection, abandonment and operator transitions use native primitives outside the production rings; no operator ring is added (reference/debugging.md).

A vref in a c2h record is a reference core retained for the host. The host releases it when it has used the record. A vref in an h2c record transfers one retained reference to core at commit. Core releases it on refusal, drop or completion; a bounce returns status, not ownership. Host retry originals belong in a bounded submission table.

Replay seeds new execution: supplied inputs derive configuration and data model values, which may differ from an earlier run. External effects are suppressed while seeding. In live execution the host may execute effects on receipt, independently of recording, persistence or c2h.macrostep_ended.

common_flags.name: replaying
common_flags.doc: part of a replay (reference/recording-and-replay.md). On c2h and tel: written by a replaying session. On h2c: an input of a replay; under a whole-system replay every h2c record carries it, sessions it spawns replay, mail between them is delivered as envelopes, and effects that would leave the process are suppressed until h2c.publish

common_flags.name: recorded
common_flags.doc: the session is recorded: its inputs appear as c2h.input

rings.name: h2c
rings.when_full: The host cannot post. It refuses at its edge (for example HTTP 503) or keeps the input itself. Core never waits on h2c.
rings.doc: Host requests, in host order. An event that cannot be admitted is consumed and bounced after its refusal output is reserved. Admission is not an execution barrier. Definition requests run between macrosteps without an envelope (reference/definitions.md).

rings.name: c2h
rings.when_full: A record an action would write does not fit: the action fails as error.execution.capacity. Core starts a macrostep only when c2h has room for all mandatory observations, cancellations, autoforwards, completion and end reports, including wrap padding. Startup and control phases can yield between macrosteps.
rings.doc: Everything that leaves the process or must not be lost: effects for I/O processors and invokers, macrostep end reports, bounces, load requests, images, and the inputs of recorded sessions.

rings.name: tel
rings.when_full: The record is dropped and counted. The next tel.dropped says how many. Telemetry never slows the system.
rings.doc: Observability: the trace records of core ADR 0067 under the existing kind masks and sampling. Never used for replay.

messages.doc: The header `at` is the new time. It never moves back. Delayed sends due by then become runnable envelopes, in due order, then send order. Applied between macrosteps. Admission of an earlier event does not ensure that event has finished; the host awaits input_completed before posting time when it requires that execution order.

messages.summary: An external event for a session
messages.doc:
Header `session` names a resident session, or is 0 and `target` gives an address. Admitted into the pool when the pool is below its watermark. An event for an unloaded address waits in the pool and core asks for the session with c2h.load_needed. A capacity refusal consumes and bounces the record, allowing later controls to progress.

A live input runs at system time when taken; its header at does not advance that clock. A replay input moves its prepared session clock at take. Complete event metadata must also fit the expanded c2h.input. Service events carry invocation_seq, checked again at take. Zero means ordinary input, or an application-supplied replay seed.

messages.doc:
With the replaying flag the session is prepared to replay (core ADR 0089): its clock starts at `clock`, it crosses no border, and it is published with h2c.publish. Inputs seed new configuration and data model values; exact restoration is not promised.

With `state`, the session is restored from a checkpoint (c2h.state, core ADR 0091) as a replaying session whose clock starts at the state's; the c2h.input records after the checkpoint follow. This is how a session survives a restart. h2c.load is not: it only pages a session back into memory within one process.

messages.summary: End a replay and put the session on the route
messages.doc:
Held delayed sends due by `at` are dropped; the rest stay in the pool under their due times (core ADR 0094). Active invocations are retired with error.communication.invoke.<id>.unavailable.

An empty `address` publishes every replaying session at once: the end of a whole-system replay (reference/recording-and-replay.md).

Refuses without mutation while supplied seed inputs remain pending. Generated local mail need not drain: pending mail follows the selected publication cut into live execution. Publication does not execute effects suppressed during seeding.

fields.name: address
fields.doc: family/name, or empty for every replaying session

fields.name: at
fields.doc: the time chosen for the seeded session

messages.doc:
Usually the answer to c2h.load_needed. Its delayed sends rejoin the pool. Waiting envelopes for it become runnable.

Loading only bounds memory; it is not persistence. The image is one c2h.unloaded wrote in this process, and it is valid only here (core ADR 0074). To restore a session after a restart, use h2c.spawn with `state` (reference/unloading.md).

Stage the complete restore outside macrosteps. Capacity or decoding failure leaves residency, timers and waiting mail unchanged. The host pins image until c2h.loaded or c2h.bounced correlates this request. Zero request_seq is refused when an active load request exists for the address.

fields.name: image
fields.doc: the bytes c2h.unloaded gave, in this process

fields.name: request_seq
fields.doc: c2h.load_needed seq; 0 for an unsolicited timer-driven load

messages.doc: Every envelope waiting for the address is recycled: mail becomes error.communication for its sender, in the same envelope (reference/envelope.md, "Recycling"); external inputs receive c2h.input_refused and DEAD_LETTER telemetry. Large waiting lists are processed incrementally between macrosteps as c2h space permits.

fields.name: request_seq
fields.doc: the outstanding c2h.load_needed seq; a stale attempt changes nothing

Refuses an owner of an active local invocation and an active locally invoked child. No lifetime envelope token moves into an image.

Refuses a session that holds a macrostep slot, including a quarantined one (bounce reason active).

Header `session` is the invoking session.

Done enters the external queue with invoke metadata for finalize; errors are platform/internal events without event invokeid. A stale live instance cannot change a later invocation with the same authored ID.

messages.doc: A session that holds a macrostep slot, running, paused or quarantined, has its execution abandoned first (core ADR 0082): c2h.macrostep_ended and c2h.input_completed say abandoned, then the session is destroyed.

messages.summary: Compile and register a complete definition
messages.doc:
Header session is 0. One atomic request, with no builder operations. Core validates a relocatable ta_scxml_spec, compiles it through the existing compiler and registers it between macrosteps. Native data model callbacks remain synchronous (reference/definitions.md).

The host keeps spec readable and diagnostic writable until the correlated c2h.definition_result. Failure registers nothing and retains nothing from the submitted spec.

fields.name: spec
fields.doc: complete declarative spec; offsets and counts, not native pointers

fields.name: datamodel
fields.doc: process-local handle of a native-installed data model adapter

fields.name: diagnostic
fields.doc: host-owned bounded output buffer for a structured compile error

messages.doc: Core ADR 0077 semantics: an unused definition is freed when its last hold, actor and nesting reference goes. Header session is 0.

fields.name: definition
fields.doc: the system-local definition ID returned by registration

messages.doc: Core ADR 0043 semantics: existing actors keep running; new spawns cannot use it. Retirement drops registration holds and is idempotent for an issued ID, including after it was freed. Header session is 0.

fields.name: definition
fields.doc: the system-local definition ID

messages.summary: Take back an admitted input that has not been taken
messages.doc:
Header session is 0. A control: it takes no envelope and is applied when read, also while core is not admitting. target_seq names an earlier h2c.event or h2c.invoke_report. If that input waits in the pool (runnable or on a waiting list), core unlinks and frees its envelope, releases its transferred values and name text, and writes c2h.input_refused with reason withdrawn. Core reserves that record before consuming the withdrawal (reference/envelope.md).

If the input is no longer waiting, the withdrawal changes nothing and writes nothing: the input already has, or will get, its own single terminal record (c2h.bounced, c2h.input_refused or c2h.input_completed). A taken input, including one paused inside its macrostep, is never withdrawn; stopping it is an operator abandon (reference/debugging.md). A target_seq not lower than this record's own seq is bounced as invalid.

fields.name: target_seq
fields.doc: the h2c seq of the input to withdraw

messages.summary: Let a quarantined session run again
messages.doc: Header session names a quarantined session. Its slot runs again where it stopped, and its chain count restarts, so a second runaway is quarantined and reported again. A control, applied when read; no debugger or exclusive ownership is needed, because a quarantined slot is at a legal boundary and runs nothing (reference/macrostep.md).

fields.name: unlimited
fields.doc: no chain limit for the rest of this input (core ADR 0075 no_microstep_limit)

messages.doc: Header session names a quarantined session. Core ADR 0082 at the slot's boundary: the configuration after the last completed microstep stays, the internal queue and the outgoing mail are freed, and effects already written stay written. The slot is free and the session takes its next input. A control, applied when read.

For a recorded session this is the first record of its log.

Creation does not imply bootstrap and invocation startup have settled. c2h.input_completed correlates that completion with the originating spawn.

fields.name: parent
fields.doc: the invoking session, or 0

fields.name: cause_seq
fields.doc: the h2c.spawn, or 0 for an <invoke>

messages.summary: A recorded session took an input
messages.doc:
Written when a recorded session takes an envelope, before any effect of the macrostep it starts. These observations, fed back as h2c.event and h2c.invoke_report under h2c.spawn(replaying), seed a new execution. Recording imposes no persistence-before-effects rule.

Not written for an input a replaying session takes: that input is already in the log being replayed. A session restored from c2h.state and replayed starts writing c2h.input again after h2c.publish.

Data is a copy_out snapshot created before binding or running the input, including finalize and autoforward. Later chart mutations cannot change it.

fields.doc: source h2c: the h2c seq

fields.name: report_ends

messages.summary: A send for an I/O processor
messages.doc:
Mail to a local session never appears here: it is an envelope (reference/envelope.md). A delayed send to an I/O processor waits in the pool and is written when due. The host may execute the send on receipt, without waiting for c2h.macrostep_ended or persistence.

A delayed send that becomes due on h2c.time is written outside any macrostep: its `macrostep` is 0, no end report follows, and the host may act on it at once. An end report would describe a macrostep that does not exist (reference/envelope.md, "A due send to an I/O processor has no macrostep end").

fields.name: macrostep
fields.doc: 0 for a delayed send that became due

fields.name: data
fields.doc: the namelist and params, aggregated by the data model

fields.name: content
fields.doc: <content>, or 0

messages.doc: Written in the post-macrostep startup phase. This record seq is the live service-instance token; authored invokeid remains the SCXML identity.

fields.name: macrostep
fields.doc: the stabilization macrostep that enabled this startup

fields.name: content
fields.doc: evaluated content, or 0

messages.doc: Mandatory state-exit output, reserved before execution. The host invalidates this instance and ignores its late callbacks.

fields.name: invocation_seq

messages.summary: Autoforward an event to an invocation
messages.doc: Every event field is preserved at the autoforward point. Finalize runs first, as in the SCXML algorithm; each recipient then receives its own copy_out data before transition code runs. Record space is mandatory; a data-model copy failure remains error.execution.

fields.name: invokeid
fields.doc: destination invocation, not the forwarded event invokeid

fields.name: invocation_seq
fields.doc: destination c2h.invoke instance

fields.name: origin_type
fields.doc: the original event origintype

fields.name: event_invokeid
fields.doc: the original event invokeid

messages.doc: Everything the macrostep wrote to c2h comes before this record. The host may already have executed effects on receipt. This record reports that execution ended and gives its status, including abandonment; invocation startup may follow. It is neither input completion nor a durability acknowledgement (reference/macrostep.md, "The macrostep end").

fields.name: source_seq
fields.doc: originating h2c input, including internal startup follow-up; 0 for local work

fields.name: effects
fields.doc: records this macrostep wrote to c2h, this end report excluded

fields.name: mail
fields.doc: envelopes it put in the pool

messages.summary: Call core back at this time
messages.doc: The earliest due delayed send in the pool changed. One timer in the host's event loop is enough.

flags.name: none
flags.doc: nothing is due: cancel the timer

messages.summary: An h2c record was not run
messages.doc: Core consumes the record, releases transferred values and keeps nothing of it. The host decides whether to retry using its own retained original. Reserve the bounded reply before consuming the request. This is terminal before admission; an admitted input instead ends in refused or completed.

messages.summary: Envelopes wait for an unloaded address
messages.doc:
Written once per address until h2c.load or h2c.load_failed answers it.

For a family whose first message creates the actor, h2c.spawn answers it.

fields.name: waiting
fields.doc: envelopes waiting for it

fields.name: cause_seq
fields.doc: the h2c.load

messages.doc:
The image holds the session's state and its delayed sends. The host keeps it, and wake_at, in its own index of unloaded sessions, and posts h2c.load when wake_at comes.

The image bounds memory; it is not a checkpoint. It is valid only in the process that wrote it and ends with it. c2h.state is the checkpoint.

fields.name: cause_seq
fields.doc: the h2c.unload

fields.name: image_bytes
fields.doc: complete valid bytes written into the requested sink

fields.name: wake_at
fields.doc: its earliest delayed send

messages.summary: A recorded session's state at a point of its log
messages.doc:
A checkpoint (core ADR 0091). Its delayed sends are inside the image, so it is one artifact. Replaying from it needs only the c2h.input records after input_seq.

Unlike the image c2h.unloaded writes, it is meant to be stored: its values are written with value_write durable=true (core ADR 0090). It is restored with h2c.spawn `state`.

fields.name: cause_seq
fields.doc: the h2c.checkpoint

fields.name: image_bytes
fields.doc: complete valid bytes written into the requested sink

fields.name: input_seq
fields.doc: the last c2h.input it includes

messages.doc: For an empty-address publication, one session-0 result summarizes the atomic mode change for all replaying sessions.

fields.name: cause_seq
fields.doc: the h2c.publish

fields.name: replayed
fields.doc: inputs it replayed; total for all-session publication

fields.name: dropped_timers
fields.doc: held delayed sends due by `at`

messages.summary: A session reached a top-level final state
messages.doc: Mail to a local parent (done.invoke) is an envelope; this record is for the host's books.
Envelopes still waiting for it are recycled as for h2c.load_failed.

fields.name: cause_seq
fields.doc: the h2c.destroy, or 0 for execution-driven destruction

messages.doc:
Exactly one result per definition request. Header session is 0. Core reserves room for this fixed-size reply before consuming the request or changing definition state. No macrostep end report follows.

A compile_error diagnostic owns copies of the code, path, subject, subject range, related text and message of ta_compile_error (core ADR 0058); no borrowed pointers escape. The host owns the buffer before and after completion (reference/definitions.md).

fields.name: cause_seq
fields.doc: the definition request’s h2c seq

fields.name: definition
fields.doc: on successful register: the definition ID; otherwise 0

fields.name: diagnostic_bytes
fields.doc: bytes written to the request’s diagnostic buffer; 0 without a compile error

messages.summary: An admitted host input was not taken
messages.doc: Exactly one terminal refusal for an admitted h2c.event or invoke_report discarded by load failure, destruction, stale-instance validation, snapshot failure or an h2c.withdraw. No input observation or completion follows. Core releases its transferred values; host retry originals remain host-owned.

fields.name: source_seq
fields.doc: the originating h2c input

messages.summary: A host input and its startup follow-up settled
messages.doc: Exactly one terminal result for a taken host input, including spawn bootstrap. Emitted after stabilization and invocation-startup internal follow-up settle, regardless of recording or replaying flags. Earlier macrostep ends do not settle the host operation. This does not hold effects, await child-service completion or acknowledge persistence.

fields.name: source_seq
fields.doc: the originating h2c input

fields.name: macrostep
fields.doc: the last macrostep in the input execution

messages.summary: A load-failure response finished recycling waiting inputs
messages.doc: Acknowledges h2c.load_failed after all waiting envelopes were recycled or refused. Each external input refusal precedes this result. Recycling may yield between macrosteps to drain c2h; its cursor uses the existing waiting list. A stale attempt receives bounced instead.

fields.name: cause_seq
fields.doc: the h2c.load_failed

fields.name: request_seq
fields.doc: the answered c2h.load_needed

messages.summary: A session reached the chain limit and is held
messages.doc: The input chain counted microstepLimit steps: microsteps, selection passes and startup passes since take. Its slot stays where it stopped and is not scheduled; its mail waits on its deferred list. If the session is a local invoked child, its direct parent gets error.communication.invoke.<id>.quarantined, without data. At most maxQuarantined slots are quarantined, never every slot; past that, core abandons the input instead and reports status runaway.

fields.name: macrostep
fields.doc: the macrostep it stopped in

fields.name: source_seq
fields.doc: the originating h2c input, or 0 for local work

fields.name: steps
fields.doc: the chain count that reached the limit

fields.name: parent
fields.doc: the parent told, or 0

messages.doc: The fields of ta_trace_record that its kind names. Values are text the data model renders (value_text), cut at the parameter telemetryValueBytes; vrefs never go on a lossy ring.

fields.name: trace_kind
fields.doc: ta_trace_kind

fields.name: position
fields.doc: ta_trace_at

fields.name: states
fields.doc: u32 state IDs: exited, entered, history, counted in the tail

flags.name: suppressed
flags.doc: an effect a replaying session did not perform

fields.name: first_seq
fields.doc: the seq the first dropped record would have had
